label: Illustrative reference data for a portfolio project. Not legal or tax advice. State base rates only; local and district taxes are not modeled.

rows.rule: Arizona use tax is owed on taxable products bought from out-of-state sellers who did not charge tax and used or consumed in Arizona.
rows.notes: Page is written for individuals; business reporting steps were not verified.

rows.rule: The state use tax rate equals the state transaction privilege tax rate, listed as 5.6 percent. Cities add their own use tax through TPT (not modeled).
Use tax does not apply to items specifically exempt from TPT, including sales for resale.

Texas use tax is owed on taxable goods and services stored, used or consumed in Texas that were bought from a seller who did not charge Texas sales tax. Permitted businesses self-report it on their regular sales tax return.
rows.notes: Page metadata date 2025-01-30. Which services are taxable was not reviewed.

rows.rule: State rate 6.25 percent; local taxes add up to 2 percent, for a combined rate up to 8.25 percent (local not modeled).
The page refers to resale or exemption certificates; it gives little detail on exemptions.
rows.notes: Thin source. Confirm on the Comptroller resale FAQ before relying on it.

rows.rule: California use tax applies to items bought from out-of-state retailers for use in California. Retailers engaged in business in the state must collect it; businesses report use tax on their sales and use tax returns.
The statewide tax rate is 7.25 percent. District taxes of 0.10 to 2.00 percent are added locally (not modeled).
A buyer purchasing for resale can avoid the tax by giving the seller a valid resale certificate.
